Your two links at the top are headings. Interactive guide-based convo here. has no text, and Try my Couples card game app based on the guide! (good for singles also!) sits over your opening: your dad's answer, why you wrote the guide, and who it's for. So the sidebar files the opening under the card game, and no reader of yours or Fable's looking for whether the advice applies to them, or how sure you are of it, found it (0 of 10 tries). In the proposals the opening has its own heading, Who This Guide Is For, with the card-game link kept as a heading just above it, named Try My Couples Card Game; then readers found it 12 of 12 tries.

# Try my Couples card game app based on the guide! (good for singles also!)
Would be

Which do you want? (a) That: both links stay headings, with the short names, and the opening gets its own (my pick, fairly sure: both links stay in the sidebar). (b) Both links become plain lines at the top, so the sidebar starts at Who This Guide Is For (the cleanest sidebar, but the links leave it). (c) The chat link stays a heading and the card-game link becomes a plain line. (d) Leave the top as it is, and pick yours or Fable's for that heading above.

Three of your # headings go straight to ### under them. The sidebar indents by level, so those sit deeper than their neighbours, and readers of every version said the levels look broken (11 of the 11 readers marked one of them or more hard). Raise each one a level, as below? It also gives each 12 pixels more room in the sidebar, and no heading's words change for it. My pick: yes, sure.

The answer to Can Casual Sex or a Situationship Actually Be Honest? sits at the end of Labels Are Descriptive, Not Prescriptive. Its last two paragraphs (“I can't decide what is okay for anybody else...” and “Outside a loving poly community or tribe, I think honest casual sex is almost impossible...”) answer the casual-sex question, and readers of every version said the labels heading sits under casual sex but reads as commitment (6 of the 11 readers marked it hard). (a) Give those two paragraphs a heading of their own, When Is It Honest?, after the labels section, so nothing moves (my pick, fairly sure). (b) Move them to the end of the casual-sex section's own text, before Situationships. (c) Leave them. Text that moves gets a Pangram check where it lands before it goes in.

The Missing Middle sits under How to find a partner. It's about a stage between being interested in someone and sleeping with them: how a relationship starts, not how to find one. Readers said it sits in the wrong place, and that it competes with Affection and the simmer for the slow stage before sex (7 of the 11 readers marked it hard). Move it to be the first section under Starting on the right foot, which has no text of its own and goes straight to the window of clarity? My pick: yes, not sure: the place is yours.
